data.narrative:
Dexterity, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Samir Menon and five co-founders, is currently valued at $1.65B post-money on $291M raised. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers in robotics and manufacturing—including Bedrock Robotics, Generalist AI, Hadrian, Agile Robots, and Nimble Robotics—plus one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implies a valuation of $3.1B. The peer-median approach across five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields $1.6B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The peer set includes two Series B companies valued at $2.0B and $1.8B, and three Series C companies spanning $1.0B to $1.6B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B (low) to $3.6B (high), with a median of $2.4B. The wide spread reflects tension between peer-median anchoring—which converges near the current valuation—and stage-progression modeling, which implies material upside. Key uncertainties include the timing and structure of the next funding round, relative market positioning versus the peer set, and near-term commercial traction. The current $1.65B valuation sits within the lower-middle of the implied range.
